newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end higher, helped by dam approval.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end higher, helped by dam approval.

text.p: Chilean shares closed higher on steady demand from overseas and gains in electrical shares following the government's licensing of a controversial dam project, brokers said.
The IPSA index of the 40 most traded shares ended 1.04 percent up at 132.12 points. The general IGPA index closed 0.86 higher to 5704.76 points on slow volume of 88 million shares traded.
Brokers reported a partial return to the strong demand from U.S. institutional investors, which drove the bourse to record heights in late May and early June.

Gains included Endesa, up 1.06 percent to 308.50 pesos. The government approved Endesa's environmental impact study for its Ralco dam project, effectively giving the final go-ahead to start building after months of delays.

Endesa's main shareholder Enersis was up 1.4 percent to 291 pesos. Other gains included several big-volume stocks that had fallen during last week's post-rally hangover and were ripe for technical rebounds. They included foodmaker Iansa, up 2.4 percent to 84 pesos and the major pulp makers. Copec was up 2.4 percent to 1880 pesos and CMPC gained 0.6 percent to 4741 pesos.

The bourse's strength this year after a stagnant 1996 was reflected in figures released by the Superintendency of Pension Fund Administrators showing marked rises in return on investments for the funds this year.

Pension funds posted a real return on investments of 1.1 percent in May and 5.5 percent in the first five months of the year, a product, "essentially of an increase in stock values," the superintendency said.
Chile's private pension fund system has deposits of $31.2 billion to end-May, up 12 percent from the same month last year, the superintendency said.
The bolsa's late upturn after flat morning trade pointed to gains on Wednesday, brokers said.
